features.name: Portuguese Empire
features.label: Brazil (Portuguese Empire)
features.source: São Vicente, founded by Martim Afonso de Sousa in 1532, was the first durable Portuguese town in Brazil; Cabral's 1500 landfall and the brazilwood factories before it are not treated as occupation.

features.name: Portuguese Empire
features.label: Brazil (Portuguese Empire)
features.source: The donatary captaincies planted lasting vilas in 1535-36 at Olinda and Igaraçu in Pernambuco, Porto Seguro, Ilhéus and Espírito Santo; the grants that failed are not drawn.

features.name: Portuguese Empire
features.label: Brazil (Portuguese Empire)
features.source: Salvador, founded in 1549 as the seat of the Governorate-General, brought royal government to Bahia; the São Vicente foothold reaches inland with the Jesuit São Paulo of 1554.

features.name: Portuguese Empire
features.label: Brazil (Portuguese Empire)
features.source: Rio de Janeiro, founded in 1565 to drive France Antarctique from Guanabara Bay, completed the sixteenth-century chain of coastal centres.

features.name: Portuguese Empire
features.label: Brazil (Portuguese Empire)
features.source: Filipéia in Paraíba (1585), São Cristóvão in Sergipe (1590) and Natal (1599) closed the gaps, so from 1600 the sugar coast is drawn continuous from Natal to Salvador; the southern captaincies remain separate coastal centres.

features.name: Portuguese Empire
features.label: Brazil (Portuguese Empire)
features.source: São Luís, taken from the French in 1615, and Belém, founded in 1616, planted the crown at the mouth of the Amazon. The Dutch-held north-east of 1630-54 is still shown Portuguese for want of a Dutch Brazil entry.

features.name: Portuguese Empire
features.label: Brazil (Portuguese Empire)
features.source: With the Dutch expelled in 1654 the settled coast is drawn continuous from Belém around to São Vicente; the interior stays outside effective settlement.

features.name: Portuguese Empire
features.label: Brazil (Portuguese Empire)
features.source: The gold strikes of the 1690s pulled settlement inland to Minas Gerais; the mining district is drawn continuous with the Rio coast.

features.name: Portuguese Empire
features.label: Brazil (Portuguese Empire)
features.source: The Treaty of Madrid of 1750 recognised Portuguese possession of the interior on uti possidetis, after the bandeirantes, Minas, Goiás and Cuiabá had carried settlement far inland; from here colonial Brazil is represented with the modern boundary until independence.

features.label: Cisplatina (Portugal)
features.source: Portuguese occupation of the Banda Oriental, later incorporated into Brazil.
